title: Long-context KV cache — reading extracts and experiment plan
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a personal scratchpad collecting quick reads, intuition notes and an experiment plan around long-context support at inference time, focused on KV cache strategies, chunked retrieval for RAG, and production constraints for Redwood’s runtime. Keep informal; will turn into a proper tech note if experiments look promising.

1) Quick summaries (papers / blogs skimmed)
- "Adaptive KV Cache for Long Sequences" (arXiv 2026): proposes tiered KV cache with LRU + relevance scoring to evict per-request keys when memory pressure rises. Key insight: use request similarity to keep high-utility keys even if older. Empirical: 2–3x generation cost reduction for chat sessions >16k tokens with <5% quality delta on summarization tasks.
- "Chunked Retrieval for RAG at Scale" (engineering blog, 2025): split documents into overlapping chunks, retrieve at chunk-level then perform late-fusion reranking on candidate windows. Helps avoid retrieving huge context blobs. Observed tradeoff: smaller chunks reduce latency and memory but increase retrieval ops and network overhead.
- "Sparse KV Routing (MoE-like) for Cache Selection" (workshop paper): embed cache keys and route queries via a light-weight top-k scorer to a subset of shards. Reduces per-step KV lookups in multi-shard setups; complexity in balancing hits across shards.
- "Quantization-aware Caching" (short note): quantized KV representations shrink memory (int8/int4) but hurt recall for near-exact-match retrieval. Suggests hybrid: store compressed values for far-history and keep recent hot keys at higher fidelity.

2) Concrete takeaways for Redwood product priorities
- Memory-first eviction policies are too crude. For Dedicated/Private customers with long-session workloads (assistant + docs), a relevance-augmented eviction (similarity + recency) will preserve head tokens that actually affect generation.
- Retrieval chunking pairs well with KV caching: store chunk-level metadata and only materialize token-level KV for top candidates. This reduces memory spikes in hosted multi-tenant setups.
- Shard-aware routing gives latency wins but needs careful admission control in the serving runtime (fallback path when shard hot).
- Quantization tradeoffs suggest offering a config knob: "kv_memory_profile": {hot: fp16, warm: int8, cold: 4-bit}, but for JSON here, idea is to prototype two-tier storage and measure generation recall.

3) Low-effort experiments to run on sandbox Dedicated pool (what I can do alone)
- Experiment A: Relevance-augmented eviction vs LRU
  - Dataset: 150 multi-turn conversations (support-agent style) truncated to 40k tokens each.
  - Configs: (a) LRU baseline, (b) recency+cosine-sim(recent-query, key)*alpha eviction score (alpha sweep 0.1/0.5/1.0)
  - Metrics: ROUGE/F1 of generated summaries vs full-context baseline, median latency, memory footprint, miss-rate (requests that required rebuilding KV).
  - Hypothesis: alpha=0.5 preserves useful context and reduces memory by ~25% with <3% quality loss.

- Experiment B: Chunked RAG + late-fusion vs monolithic retrieval
  - Setup: ingestion of 10 legal documents (avg 50k tokens) split into overlapping 2k chunks.
  - Retrieval: vector search top-50 chunks then late-fuse by passage-level reranker.
  - Compare against retrieving whole-document embeddings (vectorizing full doc) and inserting into context (if fits).
  - Metrics: end-to-end latency, tokens consumed per query, factuality (exact match on ground-truth answers).

- Experiment C: Hybrid quantized KV store (warm/cold)
  - Implement simple two-bucket store in local runtime: recent N keys in fp16, older keys in int8 (on-disk).
  - Measure decode perplexity and retrieval hit precision at different recency thresholds.

4) Implementation notes / rough pseudocode (for Owen or an infra follow-up)
- Eviction score S(key) = lambda*recency_score + (1-lambda)*relevance_score where relevance_score = max_cos_sim(key_embedding, recent_query_embeddings). On eviction, prefer removing keys with lowest S.
- For chunked retrieval, store metadata: chunk_id, doc_id, chunk_bounds, sparse_topic_vector, small summary. At request time: retrieve top-K chunk_ids, expand to token KV only for top-M chunks.
- Shard-aware routing: maintain light-weight bloom filter of hot keys/model for each shard; query top-3 shards by score and fallback to global path if misses.

5) Evaluation plan / dashboards to create (Console hooks)
- Per-session KV hit-rate over time (sliding window), broken down by eviction policy and model size.
- Quality delta alerts: when rerun on held-out prompt set, if Rouge/QA drops >5% after rollout, trigger rollback.
- Cost dashboard: tokens saved per session by caching vs cost of extra rerank/retrieval ops.

6) Risks / open questions
- Complexity: relevance scoring implies computing embeddings for recent queries; must be careful of CPU bottlenecks. Should we approximate with hashed signatures?
- Consistency: in dedicated pools with autoscaling, shard membership can change — need atomic handoff of warm/hot KV.
- Privacy: for Private deployments, storing compressed cold keys on shared disk may have implications; tie to KMS/HSM if encrypted at rest.

7) Next steps (short list)
- Prototype Experiment A in local dev Dedicated pool (I can set up dataset + runner): target 2-week sprint.
- Sync with Owen on shard routing feasibility and Hannah on quantized storage serialization format.
- Draft a short tech note for product describing "KV caching profiles" that could be surfaced in Redwood Console as a tuning suggestion.

Notes to self (loose)
- Try alpha sweep values = [0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 1.0].
- Remember to log token-level cost delta, not just latency. Users care about $/response.
- Link to prior SRE runbook for cache pressure events (JIRA-OPS-67).

References read (quick):
- Adaptive KV Cache paper, arXiv 2026 (see linked_artifacts)
- Chunked RAG blog (engineering)
- Workshop note on sparse KV routing
- Internal PR: kv-proto/pull/87 (serialization change)

End of scratchpad. Will refine after first experiment results.
